html:
The Gwa'sala and 'Nakwaxda'xw are two Kwakwaka'wakw peoples of the central British Columbia coast, whose homes were Smith Inlet and Seymour Inlet, north of Vancouver Island. They speak Kwak'wala, one of the Wakashan languages.

Like their neighbours the Da'naxda'xw, they fished salmon and eulachon and held the potlatch. In 1964 the Canadian government moved both peoples from their villages to a small reserve at Tsulquate, near Port Hardy, promising housing that was not ready. The move broke their ties to their lands and is remembered as one of the most damaging relocations in British Columbia. The two now form one nation in Canada.
